name: SW-520D tilt sensor module
description: Tilt detector: an SW-520D ball tilt switch and an LM393 comparator with a sensitivity potentiometer. The ball closes the switch while the module stands upright, so DO is LOW when upright and goes HIGH once the module is tilted past roughly 15-45 degrees; the DO LED lights while upright. Open-collector LM393 output with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: SW-520D tilt sensor module (common blue 3-pin LM393 clone board: VCC, GND, DO).
eli5: Tells your board when it is tipped over, like a tiny spirit level that only says 'standing' or 'tipped'.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (pin 1). With a 3.3 V board connect it to 3V3, because DO is pulled up to VCC.

pins.name: DO
pins.description: Digital output (pin 3): LOW while upright, HIGH while tilted (pulled up to VCC by 10 kOhm)

buildNotes: Header order as printed: VCC, GND, DO.
On an ESP32 or Pico power VCC from 3V3: the board's pull-up takes DO to VCC, so a 5 V supply puts 5 V on the GPIO.
DO is LOW while the gold switch can points up (upright) and HIGH when tilted. Check the polarity on your board once: the DO LED is lit when DO is low.
Mount the module with the switch can vertical, leads down, for the 'upright' reference position.
The ball bounces as it rolls; the driver waits for the level to settle before reporting a change.

example.code:
from sw520d import SW520D
import time

sensor = SW520D({DO})
while True:
    print('Tilt: %s' % ('TILTED' if sensor.tilted() else 'upright'))
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports a tilt when the sensor is tipped over

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
